setup.subtitle: See which landing places keep sunlight for power and Earth in view for radio contact through your whole stay.

where.label: Where do you want to land?
where.coordsHint: Coordinates: latitude, then longitude, in degrees. South and west are minus.
where.coordsError: Write the latitude (−90 to 90), a comma, then the longitude (−180 to 180).
where.error: Pick a known site or enter your own coordinates.

when.label: When do you want to land?

stay.label: How long will the mission stay on the Moon?

hero.alt: The full Moon, a NASA visualization made from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data
hero.credit: Moon image: NASA Goddard, made from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data.

screen.error: Some of the data did not load, so a place may be missing. Check your connection, then reload the page.
screen.mapHint: Each line points from a place toward the Sun or Earth at the time shown.

terrain.label: Hills
terrain.on: Counted: the real horizon, with its hills and dips

copyLink.failed: Copy failed. Copy the link from the address bar.

picker.addHint: See up to 3 places side by side for the same dates.

site.loading: Working out where the Sun and Earth will be…
site.typedBody: We cannot work out results for typed coordinates yet. Add a known place to compare instead.
site.unknownBody: This place is not on our list, so there is nothing to show for it.
site.missingBody: We have no hills data for this place yet. Switch Hills to Ignored to see it with a flat horizon.

caveat.terrainNotModeled: Hills are not mapped for this place, so its horizon is treated as flat. On the real ground the Sun and Earth may come and go at other times.
caveat.approximate: Approximate location: this point stands for a wider region.
caveat.horizonIncomplete: Hills beyond the edge of our height map are not counted, so the Sun and Earth may be hidden more often than shown.
caveat.terrainOff: Hills are ignored, so this shows a perfectly flat horizon. On the real ground the Sun and Earth come and go at other times.

fit.fitsReason: During your stay there is never more than 50 hours in a row without the Sun or Earth in view.
fit.riskyReason: No Sun and no Earth from {{from}} until {{to}}. That is more than 50 hours in a row.

stay.day: Checked for a stay of about 1 day.
stay.threeDays: Checked for a stay of about 3 days.
stay.week: Checked for a stay of about a week.
stay.twoWeeks: Checked for a stay of about 14 days.
stay.month: Checked for a stay of one full Moon day (29.5 days).

horizon.title: The sky from here
horizon.label: Panorama from {{site}}: the hills along the horizon, with the Sun and Earth.
horizon.legend: Thin lines: where the Sun and Earth travel over the time span shown. Grey: the ground and hills.
horizon.scale: Height shown: {{range}}° above and below level ground.

countdown.title: What happens next
countdown.sunStaysUp: The Sun stays in view for a Moon day or longer
countdown.sunStaysDown: The Sun stays hidden for a Moon day or longer
countdown.earthStaysUp: Earth stays in view for a Moon day or longer
countdown.earthStaysDown: Earth stays hidden for a Moon day or longer

metrics.title: The numbers
metrics.blackout: Longest time with no Sun and no Earth
metrics.sunVisible: How much of the Sun is visible now
metrics.overLunarDay: of the Moon day from landing (29.5 days)
metrics.inLunarDay: in the Moon day from landing (29.5 days)
metrics.aboveLevel: above level ground, at the time shown
metrics.belowLevel: below level ground, at the time shown

timeline.title: When the Sun and Earth are in view
timeline.legend: Bars: in view. Gaps: hidden. Both: the Sun and Earth in view together. The frame marks your stay.
timeline.summary_one: {{lane}}: in view {{count}} time in this time span.
timeline.summary_other: {{lane}}: in view {{count}} times in this time span.

playback.hint: Arrow keys move 1 hour. Shift and an arrow key move 1 day.

credits.title: Where the data comes from
credits.positions: Sun and Earth positions: astronomy-engine, checked against NASA JPL Horizons to within 0.01°.
credits.hills: Hills: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA polar height maps (LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, PDS Geosciences Node), seen from 2 metres above the ground.
credits.checks: Checked against PGDA 69 (Mazarico et al. 2011, average sunlight at the poles). Reference height map: PGDA 90 (Barker et al. 2023).

map.label: Map of the Moon's south pole with a marker for each place you picked
map.labelEmpty: Map of the Moon's south pole. No places picked yet.
map.image: Shaded relief of the Moon's south pole
map.lowerBound: Hills beyond the height map are not counted, so the Sun and Earth may be hidden more often than shown.
map.offMap: {{site}} is too far from the pole to show on this map.
map.credit: Terrain: NASA LRO LOLA height map, shaded for display.
